selection.rationale: Re-select the same region (ResNetEmbeddings + all four ResNetBasicLayer groups) and repair the previous trial's concrete numerical failure. Measured facts: clean median latency_ms is 4.225017 (project.json original_baseline) while the 88 CUDA kernels of one forward sum to 4152.3 us (call-resources.json, root call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 rank 0), so the window is GPU-bound with ~73 us of host headroom; the python_runtime collector corroborates (its cProfile window is dominated by torch._C._cuda_synchronize self 1.646 ms, with all nn.Module _call_impl/_wrapped_call_impl/__getattr__ wrapper cost ~0.43 ms under perturbation and overlapped in clean runs), so host-side plays (CUDA graphs, Python trimming) stay rejected - the binding contract additionally notes CUDA Graph replay does not rerun the Python hooks that quality coverage counts. Kernel composition of the 4152.3 us: conv math ~3045.6 us (73.3%, frozen: FP32, TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark off; ampere scudnn/winograd variants already selected), eager pointwise 889.7 us (21.4%: 20x cudnn::bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel_NCHW = 425.4 us; 25x vectorized_elementwise covering 17 relu clamps + 8 CUDAFunctor residual adds = 464.3 us), max_pool_forward_nchw 198.2 us. The transformers 5.16.1 structure inside this region (modeling_resnet.py:65-69,85-93,113-136) runs each conv into a separate BN pass, a separate ReLU pass, and per block a separate residual add plus second ReLU - up to 5 full-tensor memory-bound passes per block for what is one elementwise expression y = relu(bn_affine(conv2(conv1(x))) + shortcut(x)); collapsing these to one pass per chain attacks exactly the 889.7 us pool. The edits are interdependent (block conv2's BN must fuse with the block-level add+ReLU; the stem BN with the stem ReLU), so this is one coherent region, not independent group edits; the 9 module boundaries give the replacement ownership of the fused chains while convs, the stem max-pool and the 3 shortcut conv+BN modules keep their observed parent dispatch. Concrete failure repaired (previous-feedback.txt + previous-candidate/candidate.py, not a re-explanation of a category): the trial ran and dispatch worked (run passed, all 9 required call sites invoked 2x, binding 'direct', coverage complete) but quality failed with 32000/32000 mismatches and max_abs_error 40.84. Root cause 1, causal from the code: the Triton kernels index a contiguous NCHW tensor as channel-major, base = c*hw with hw = N*H*W, so element offset c*(N*H*W)+linear lands in true channel (c*N + n) mod C - the per-channel BN affine constants a,b were applied to scrambled channels, and the route telemetry shows all 8 blocks executed 'triton_fused_bn_add_relu' with no fallback, so the corrupted output reached the logits; this is an indexing bug, not inherent fusion error, and the fix is to tile over [N*C, H*W] planes with true channel = plane % C (or decompose n,c explicitly). Root cause 2: the stem guard compared the 3-channel input against the 64-channel BN constants (int(x.shape[1]) != channels), so the stem always raised _Fallback (diagnostic event candidate.py:147, count 2) and silently ran the parent - the guard must compare input channels to num_channels and conv output channels to the BN size, otherwise the stem fusion is forfeited. Both bugs are in the rejected candidate only; the region boundary, parent/module dispatch and coverage model are proven viable by the same failed run. Alternatives rejected on measured evidence: cudnn.benchmark/TF32 (frozen numerical policy), channels_last (frozen NCHW batch semantics), host-side or graph capture (GPU-bound window + coverage semantics). Communication analysis is not applicable (single device, resources.json).
selection.hypothesis: Replace the forward of ResNetEmbeddings and the 8 ResNetBasicLayer modules (region groups as in the previous trial, same current-discovery IDs) with corrected fused pointwise chains: conv1/conv2/stem conv stay on the observed parent Conv2d dispatch (cudnn kernels, bit-identical outputs); each chain then runs one Triton kernel - y = max(fma(x, a_c, b_c), 0) and y = max(fma(z, a_c, b_c) + s, 0) with a = weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b = bias - mean*a packed once at installation - with NCHW-correct indexing: grid over [N*C, H*W] planes, per-plane channel index pid % C addressing A/B, replacing the previous channel-major base = c*(N*H*W) scrambling that caused the 40.8 max_abs_error quality failure; the stem eligibility guard is fixed to check the 3-channel input against num_channels and the 64-channel conv output against the BN size so the stem actually fuses instead of falling back. Expected effect on the objective: the 42 eager pointwise launches (20 BN + 17 ReLU + 8 add, 889.7 us at ~0.9-1.4 TB/s effective) collapse to 17 single-pass kernels, cutting full-tensor traffic from 11 passes/block to 5 and 2 to 1 in the stem, so the pointwise pool should shrink to ~380-450 us and latency_ms from 4.225 to ~3.75-3.90 ms (-8 to -12%); the now-unblocked stem BN+ReLU fusion adds a small extra beyond the previous (never-measured, fallback-only) stem contribution. Numerics: conv outputs unchanged; the fused affine uses the same eval-BN formula with FMA-order differences of ~1 ULP per element, far below atol/rtol 1e-4, but this remains a hypothesis the framework's paired logits check and require_exact_top1 must confirm on the GPU - the previous trial's 40.8 error was the indexing bug and says nothing about the true fused drift. Unknowns to test rather than assume: top-2 logit gap sensitivity of the 3 fixture images under the drift; whether Triton JIT compilation lands fully in quality/warmup execution outside the 5 timed samples; whether packed derived constants (checkpoint parameters never mutated) are accepted under the frozen no-weight-change invariant; and whether the memory goal is preserved (fused outputs replace equal-sized intermediates, ~19 KB of packed constants added). Only the measured median latency_ms credits the gain.

proposal.rationale: Same region and 9 module boundaries as trial-77617c1424 (ResNetEmbeddings + all 8 ResNetBasicLayer sites, groups 3821cceac23fa97e5a55/5233e425bbe8203a4dc0/5eb0dee1d36938317bbe/c1271430eda49ac23557/9f7c0638f7c2fd3e7c50; IDs re-verified against the current discovery in targets.json), with the two concrete defects that failed quality repaired. Diagnosis of the prior failure from previous-feedback: max_abs_error 40.837 with 32000/32000 logits mismatched (100%) is a data-placement error, not FMA drift; the prior Triton kernels launched grid axis 1 as channel index c and computed the plane base c*(N*H*W), i.e. channel-major indexing, while a contiguous NCHW tensor is batch-major (element (n,ch,h,w) at (n*C+ch)*H*W + h*W + w), so every channel/batch pair was scrambled. Repair 1: the kernels now enumerate N*C output planes on grid axis 1; plane p covers the contiguous span [p*H*W,(p+1)*H*W) and indexes the packed affine vectors by channel = p % C. Repair 2: the prior stem guard required x.shape[1]==num_channels(3) AND x.shape[1]==channels(64) simultaneously (coverage evidence: 'parent_fallback_guard' x2, reference_invocations 683c...x2), an unsatisfiable condition that made the stem silently fall back; it now checks the input against num_channels and the conv output against the BN size, so the stem actually fuses. Conv1/conv2/stem conv/stem MaxPool2d/shortcut conv+BN stay on the observed parent module dispatch (cudnn kernels, bit-identical outputs); each chain then runs one Triton kernel, y=max(fma(x,a,b),0) and y=max(fma(z,a2,b2)+s,0), with a=weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b=bias-mean*a packed once at installation. CPU validation of this attempt (no GPU touched): the kernels under TRITON_INTERPRET match torch relu(a*x+b) and relu(a*z+b+s) bit-exactly including a channel-mapping canary the old bug fails, and a full-model walk of the real pretrained weights through build()'s replacements reproduces the parent logits to 3.8e-06 max abs (tolerance 1e-4) with equal argmax and all 9 sites reporting fused routes. Expected effect (from the selection's measured composition: 88 forward kernels sum 4152.3us vs 4.2250ms median, so GPU-bound with ~73us host headroom; host-side plays and CUDA Graph replay stay rejected - replay would not rerun the Python hooks quality coverage counts): the 42 eager pointwise launches (20 BN 425.4us + 17 ReLU 343.9us + 8 add 120.4us = 889.7us) collapse to 17 single-pass kernels, cutting full-tensor traffic from 11 passes/block and 2 in the stem to 5 and 1, targeting the pointwise pool at ~380-450us and latency_ms 4.225 -> ~3.75-3.90ms (-8 to -12%), with the stem fusion now contributing rather than falling back. Numerics remain the same eval-BN affine the native cudnn bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel evaluates, with only rsqrt/FMA ordering differences of ~1 ULP per element; final arbiter is the framework's paired logits check (atol/rtol 1e-4) and require_exact_top1 on the leased GPU.
proposal.setup_work: build() runs once at installation, before validation, on the modules from context['modules']. Per physical module: structural verification (Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/Identity/MaxPool2d types, eval mode, affine BN with running stats), then one-time packing of eval-BN affine constants a=weight*rsqrt(running_var+eps), b=bias-running_mean*a for the 17 fused BNs (stem + 2 per block) as contiguous float32 device tensors computed under torch.no_grad from the live parameters: 34 tensors of at most 512 floats each, ~19 KB device memory total, retained for the module lifetime. Checkpoint parameters are never mutated (derived, detached copies only; verified by a parameter checksum in the CPU walk) and nothing fixture-dependent is precomputed. Triton JIT compiles lazily at first launch: 2 kernels x 3 BLOCK variants (64/256/1024 chosen per plane size H*W) = 6 compilations, landing in the framework's quality/coverage execution and the 2 warmup calls, ahead of the 5 timed samples; compilation is in-process cached and the timed window then launches only steady-state kernels. No CUDA Graph capture is used, so no retained graph pools are introduced and no invocation-boundary work is moved outside run(); Triton module loading is driver allocation outside the PyTorch allocator counters and no claim is made about it. Setup allocations and timing appear in the installation receipt.
quality_risks: FMA/rounding order differs from the native cudnn BN kernel and the separate add kernel by ~1 ULP per element (rsqrt(var+eps), fma(x,a,b) vs fl(fl(x*a)+b), and the (+s) rounding position); the full-model CPU walk measured 3.8e-06 max logit deviation, well under atol/rtol 1e-4, but the bound on GPU is confirmed only by the framework's paired logits comparison.

require_exact_top1: an argmax flip needs a top-2 logit gap below the fused drift (~1e-5 absolute); unlikely for the three pinned fixture images (CPU walk shows identical argmax), but it is a discrete failure mode only the GPU check can confirm.
tl.maximum(v, 0.0) maps NaN to 0 (IEEE fmax) whereas aten::relu propagates NaN; only relevant for non-finite activations, which the pinned finite FP32 fixture and weights do not produce.

Triton availability: triton 3.7.1 ships with the pinned torch 2.13.0+cu129 worker; if import or first launch fails, every affected call falls back to the parent forward via context['references'] with 'setup_fallback_parent'/'parent_fallback_error' route labels, preserving correctness at baseline speed; guard trips on unexpected signatures report 'parent_fallback_guard'.
First-invocation JIT compilation (6 variants, seconds) lands in quality/warmup execution outside the 5 timed samples; acknowledged as setup cost the framework observes.

The parent's in-place hidden_state += residual is replaced by an out-of-place fused write; this is alias-equivalent because the += target (the conv2-BN output) is block-local, never aliased outside the block, and the block input is read-only in both implementations (guard fallback result verified identical to the parent on CPU).

Peak allocated bytes may fall slightly because two fused intermediates replace five per-block temporaries; that is a per-run allocation-lifecycle counter change, not a general physical-memory saving, and setup adds ~19 KB of retained packed constants.
